title: Sri Akal Takht Sahib denies approval to Raj Kundra’s proposed film ‘Nihang’
text:
Sri Akal Takht Sahib denies approval to Raj Kundra’s proposed film ‘Nihang’ | Punjab Newsline Friday, 20 November 2026 Regional Excellence • Global Reach RSS Feed About Contact Trending National Punjab Haryana Himachal Chandigarh Other States Regional Portals Delhi NCR Uttar Pradesh Jammu & Kashmir Uttarakhand Political Business Opinion Films & TV Home Trending National Punjab Haryana Himachal Chandigarh Other States Regional Portals Delhi NCR Uttar Pradesh Jammu & Kashmir Uttarakhand Political Business Opinion Films & TV Videos Photos Trending Home Films & TV Sri Akal Takht Sahib denies approval to Raj Kundra’s proposed film ‘Nihang’
 Updated on: 20 Nov 2026 Punjab Newsline | Amritsar 
 Sri Akal Takht Sahib has denied granting any approval to filmmaker Raj Kundra for his proposed film ‘Nihang’, dismissing reports suggesting that the project had received the religious body's consent.
 The clarification was issued by the Sri Akal Takht Secretariat following discussions surrounding the alleged approval. The secretariat categorically stated that Acting Jathedar Singh Sahib Giani Kuldeep Singh Gargajj had not granted Raj Kundra permission to make the film.
 According to a statement issued by the secretariat, Kundra had visited the Sri Akal Takht Sahib Secretariat some time ago and presented his ideas regarding the proposed film before the Jathedar. However, describing the meeting as an approval or endorsement of the project is incorrect and misleading.
 Bagicha Singh, in-charge of the Sri Akal Takht Sahib Secretariat, said that the Jathedar had listened to Kundra's views during the meeting. He was also handed a copy of the directive issued by the five Sikh high priests on December 28, 2025, regarding the production of films based on Sikh history.
 The directive clearly prohibits the creation of films, animated movies and AI-generated videos depicting Sikh Gurus, their family members, historical Sikh warriors and martyrs through imitations or portrayals of their physical appearances.
 The order further highlighted the challenges posed by modern technology to Sikh identity, traditions, principles and philosophy. It stressed the need to preserve and promote traditional methods of religious propagation through the Sakhi tradition, Gurdwaras and Sikh institutions.
 The secretariat's clarification makes it clear that Raj Kundra's visit and presentation of his film concept should not be interpreted as official approval from Sri Akal Takht Sahib.
